info.title: OpenAsy Passwords API
info.summary: A password manager for the team on Vaultwarden, with shared vaults by Identity group.
info.description:
Every screen of Passwords uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

The shared vaults, who may see or change each, and the policies are set in the vaults file, never through the API; Passwords keeps Vaultwarden in step with it and with Identity. Under `/api/v1/vault` a signed-in person's browser reaches Vaultwarden through this server, as it is: the browser derives every key and decrypts every item, and this server keeps none of them. Those routes take the session of that person, never an API token. Everything else takes a session or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: user, viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.description: Adds an item the browser encrypted: to the person's own vault through Vaultwarden's /api/ciphers, or to shared vaults through /api/ciphers/create when collectionIds is not empty. `cipher.organizationId` is null or the company's organization; `cipher.encryptedFor` is the person's Vaultwarden user id. Vaultwarden checks that they may write to those collections. Needs a signed-in person, not an API token.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Passwords runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Passwords origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings, API tokens (`oa_passwords_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Passwords is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

error.description: Why the file on disk is not applied; the last good version stays in use.

vaults.description: Vault ids whose access was set again.

missing.description: Vault ids with no collection in Vaultwarden yet; an admin's browser creates them.

members.description: Confirmed members; null before the first sync.

keyHolders.description: Confirmed owners and admins, who hold the organization's key; with none, the shared vaults cannot be opened again.

deviceType.description: Bitwarden's device type: 2 Chrome extension, 9 Chrome, 1 iOS and so on.

itemId.description: Vaultwarden's id of the item; the browser decrypts its name.

vaults.description: Vault ids of the file, or collection ids for collections the file does not name.

lastOpened.description: When the leaver last opened, copied or filled it in.

recent.description: Opened in the last 90 days: change it first.

changed.description: Marked as changed, or its password changed after the leaver was known.

reason.description: planned: an editor set the date; disabled: Identity disabled them; no-group: they left every group of the file; gone: Identity no longer lists them.

generator.description: The vaults file's passwordGenerator policy, which passwords made in the pages follow.

VaultwardenAnswer.description: Vaultwarden's own answer (its API is Bitwarden's). Keys and items in it are encrypted; only the person's browser decrypts them.
